We need to simulate three experts collaborating, but final output: a complete JUnit 4 test file with start/end markers. Should include tests for all public methods: constructor, clone, serialize(Serializable, OutputStream), serialize(Serializable), deserialize(InputStream), deserialize(byte[]). Also test edge cases: null inputs, exception handling (e.g., serialization of non-serializable object -> should throw SerializationException), IOException during serialization? Might be hard to simulate, but we can use a custom OutputStream that throws IOException on close/write to test exception. Also test ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream's resolveClass fallback. Could create a class with custom classloader? Probably too heavy; we can test that deserialize works for an object whose class is loaded by a different classloader, but not necessary.

We'll write tests using JUnit 4: @Test, expected exceptions.

Need to import necessary classes: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert.*, maybe org.junit.rules.ExpectedException.

Define a simple Serializable class (e.g., Person) with fields, equals, hashCode.

Test clone: clone null returns null; clone a Person returns equal but not same reference; clone an object that throws NotSerializableException? Actually clone requires Serializable; if we pass a non-serializable object compile error. So test with a Serializable that contains non-serializable field (transient) maybe still works. Use an object that is Serializable but its class has no-arg constructor.

Test serialize to OutputStream: valid case writes bytes; null OutputStream throws IllegalArgumentException; also test that serialize with null object writes null (ObjectOutputStream writes null reference). Then verify that deserialization returns null.

Test serialize(Serializable) returns non-empty byte array for non-null; returns byte array that can be deserialized to same object.

Test deserialize(InputStream): null stream throws IllegalArgumentException; valid stream returns object; also test deserialization of corrupted bytes causing SerializationException.

Test deserialize(byte[]): null array throws IllegalArgumentException; valid array works; corrupted array throws SerializationException.

Test ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream fallback: we can create a custom classloader that cannot load a class, but thread context can. Use a simple class defined in current classloader; create a custom classloader that delegates to parent only for java.* but not for our class, causing ClassNotFoundException inside resolveClass, then fallback to thread context. Setting thread context classloader to default. Then deserialize using clone (which uses this class). Should succeed.

We'll also test that the close exceptions are ignored (hard to assert). Not needed.
